In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kudzu vine is a source of a variety of C-glycosylated isoflavones.

the KDS analyzed in this work is a source of puerarin and daidzein, and to a lesser extent of other isoflavones, such as daidzein-7-O-beta-D-glucopyranoside, daidzin, daidzein 7-O-beta-D-apiosyl-(1-3)-beta-D-glucopyrannoside, and puerarin 7-O-beta-glucoside.
the isoflavonoid composition of KDS is highly variable, and the concentration of isofavonoids in KDS is dependent on the extraction method and extraction solvent.

MS/MS is a powerful technique for profiling and characterization of isomeric compounds in kudzu supplements.
MS/MS is a very powerful technique to characterize isoflavonoid glycosides and to detect the presence of other C- or O-glycosylated compounds in kudzu.

the HPLC-DAD and LC-MS/MS methods developed in this study are suitable for the analysis of isoflavoids in kudzus and their dietary supplements, and the results of this study will be useful in the quality control of these products.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of negative ionization MS/MS in combination with neutral loss scans is a powerful tool for the detection of isoflavone C-glycosyls.
the HPLC-MS/MS method can provide useful data on the isoflavonoid profile in kudzu extracts and supplements.
